recipes.name: Buffalo Chicken Chili
ingredients_raw: 1 large carrot, peeled and finely chopped
0.5 cup hot buffalo wing sauce (such as Frank's® REDHOT Buffalo Wing Sauce), or to taste
1 (15 ounce) can white kidney or cannellini beans, drained
1 (19 ounce) can red kidney beans, drained

steps.text: Heat olive oil and butter in a large pot over medium-high heat. Place chicken in the pot. Cook and stir until chicken is no longer pink, 7 to 10 minutes.
Stir in carrot, onion, celery, garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, salt, and pepper. Cook and stir until onion is translucent and carrots begin to soften, 3 to 4 more minutes.

Stir in hot sauce, tomato sauce, crushed tomatoes, and white and red kidney beans. Bring to a boil, then simmer over medium-low heat until vegetables are tender and flavors have blended, about 1 hour.

raw_recipe.headline: Buffalo Chicken Chili
raw_recipe.description: This Buffalo chicken chili has the zing of Buffalo wings. Serve at your game day party.

review.reviewBody: I made this in advance for super bowl but my husband and adult children wanted to have it for super that night because it smelt so good and the taste was even greater. I did not alter one thing, I will warn you that it is hot but that was why I wanted to make it in the first place and it didn't let me down.

I am pleasantly suprised by this recipe, although I did modify it quite a bit. As suggested in other reviews I used chicken breast, only 2 tbsp chili powder, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 can of tomato sauce, increased then franks wing sauce to 3/4 cup, added 1/4 cup franks traditional hot sauce and 1/4 tsp celery seed. I cooked the chicken and sauce in the slow cooker all day, then added the veggies when I got home from work, and cooked on hight for an additional half hour. Served with baked tortilla chips from this side. With the modifications this was VERY Buffalo-y! Mmm!!!

New favourite Chilli recipe. Basically followed the recipe,with a few tweaks. We love hot so I added: more Frank's, red pepper flakes, diced tomatoes with chilies, and a little more chilli powder. I thought, as like most of the reviews, it looked a little thin so I added some tomato paste. Still too thin, busted out my favourite thickening agent: a teaspoon ( for about a gallon of chilli) xanthan gum. One teaspoon was all it took to tighten it right up.

Very tasty. Won a chili cookoff with this! Doubled (tripled?) the garlic, used about 3/4 c Franks hot sauce (not the buffalo sauce), shredded chicken breasts, and added a little cream cheese. Slow cooked for 9 hours.

What an awesome idea! I really wanted it to taste like buffalo so based on other reviews and what I had on had. I used 2 lbs boneless chicken breasts coated with hot sauce, garlic powder, and cayenne baked and shredded instead of ground chicken. I used more carrot, less chili powder, and no cumin. Added 1 cup of frank's hot sauce (not wing), 1 can of tomato sauce, 1 can of diced tomatoes with roasted garlic simmered that for 30 mins, then added the shredded chicken, and 1 can of cannellini beans. 3 cups water and 2 T tomato paste gave the right thickeness and simmered an additional 30 mins. Served with blue cheese on top

This is a really good chili!!! Followed a few suggestions and cut the spices in half to begin with. I didn't want it to be too intense for the kiddos. I ended up using a 1/2 c of Franks because I too was looking for more of a hot wing flavor, and for personal preference I used black beans instead of white.
This was a hit. And because my boys were looking for something more along the lines of like a hot wing dip, I melted a little cream cheese into theirs. Holy cow!!! Now that was some good stuff!
Cut hot sauce in half! (Can add a cup of heavy whipping cream at the end, Allen loved it).

This was a nice change of pace. I opted to turn it into a crock pot recipe by tossing everything into the crock pot, along w/2 BLSL chicken breasts (which I pulled and shredded when they were done). Mr. LTH is a sissy when it comes to spice, so I decreased the chili powder to 3 T and a little less Frank's. I love spice and this was still spicy enough for me and Mr. LTH just deemed it "very good". I subbed diced tomatoes for one of the cans of sauce to give it more texture and left out the celery per personal preference. Thanks for the recipe, Lisa!

AMAZING recipe. I was going for a buffalo chicken flavor and ended up with the perfect combination of chili flavor and buffalo sauce.

I ended up using about .8 cups of buffalo sauce, only 3 (heaping) tablespoons of chili powder, and replaced half of the crushed tomatoes with diced tomatoes mixed with green chili peppers.

I threw my soup pot in the oven for a couple of hours instead of cooking it on the stove (don't have to stir as much this way). All the roommates were extremely happy with the results and this will be a repeated recipe.

Very good, but I did make a few changes to make it even easier. I made it in the crock pot and I used boneless chicken breasts. I put them in the crock pot raw, then dumped the rest of the ingredients on top. The chicken will cook with the chili. after about 5 hours I removed the chicken, shredded it and put it back in the pot to simmer a few more hours. I also left out the carrot.

I won two First Place prizes out of four at a chili cook off with this! I beat out culinary professionals, restaurants, and individuals alike! People were coming back for thirds and fourths! Had competitors coming over because they heard how good it was from others! I made mine in a crockpot, and I added more/different stuff than what the recipe calls for. I added mushrooms, red/yellow/orange/green bell peppers, squash and zucchini. I shredded the chicken so everyone would get some in their cup. I made a sweet cornbread to accompany it and to offset any heat. I had ranch, bleu cheese, sour cream, shredded sharp cheddar, and mini celery sticks to be added at the tasters choice. People kept coming up to me asking which restaurant I was representing, and it felt so good to just say "myself"! I could t have been more proud of my chili and myself!
This was delicious and very easy to make! I’m happy to have this as a variation for chili. It definitely has a kick to it, so keep that in mind if you don’t like too much spice.

I doubled the chicken wing sauce to 1 cup of Franks "Mild" Chicken wing sauce and backed off to 4 TBLSP of the chili powder. I would encourage people to experiment with their favorite wing sauce. Next try will be a garlic parmesan wing sauce for us. Thanks Dan
Easy and quick prep and very tasty I did add an extra pound of chicken and a can of black beans. Yummy
Excellent chili! I omitted the beans and added some capers and diced poblano. Served with crumbled bleu cheese and crushed tortilla chips for some crunch. A winner to be sure!

I saved this recipe year ago & make it several times a year. Usually when we have company for a game or a fall birthday party, etc.. Everyone loves it. It is always a hit. The only downside is there's never any leftover for the next day.

I thought this recipe was very good. It made a good variation of chili to add to the mix! The only changes I made were to use just white beans and actually doubled the amount of Red Hot. I don't understand the reviews that complain it's too spicy. If something has Red Hot in the ingredient list, there's your indication it's going to be spicy!
I topped it with crumbled bleu cheese. I also used mushrooms in place of beans to make it more keto friendly for my sister. And you don't miss the beans.
My teen and I love it. It's sweet and spicy. I used one can of tomato sauce, one can of stewed tomatoes, and one can of kidney beans. In the final 10 minutes, I added canned corn.
I made it without the beans and without some of the veggies and subbed the meat for turkey. It was amazing! Everyone loved it and didn't even notice the absence of beans or that I used turkey!
